Adding ~80 LoC of subtype scaffolding for a 6-line consumer is overkill; the sealed subtypes would mirror the same boolean combinations the new field captures, ironically reintroducing the "lifecycle as flags" smell at the type level. The sealed approach pays off for player-facing lifecycles (multi-surface, multi-state UI) — not for a private evaluator output read by one orchestrator. B) Stay with the enum and just type the engine's matcher (`r.state == NodeState.completed` instead of `r.state.name == 'completed'`). Rejected: addresses the string-compare smell but leaves the redundant enum tag in place, perpetuating the V2-origin debt R.2 was scoped to retire. C) Replace `state` with separate `isCompleted` / `isLocked` / `isAvailable` booleans. Rejected: the three are mutually exclusive and derivable from `eligibleByConditions` + `completed`; storing all three would invite drift (a future edit setting `isLocked: true` AND `isCompleted: true`) and reintroduce the flag-soup anti-pattern. One boolean + the existing eligibility flag is the minimal sufficient representation.

decisions.title: R.3.a — Journey map widget-no-logic sweep via documented lint-ignore
decisions.context: Phase 19 (UI sweep) time-boxed widget-no-logic cleanup to two features (quests + cosmetics). `lib/features/journey/presentation/widgets/journey_interactive_map.dart` (1200 LoC) was left with 9 collection-logic hits — five flagged in the original Track A scoping note plus four more surfaced by the full scan. The journey feature has no `application/` layer: `JourneyAdapter` (a static helper that lives in `presentation/widgets/`) consumes `ProgressionEngineProvider` directly and produces a flat `List<JourneyCheckpoint>` of presentation VOs with pre-computed display-state flags (`isPathAnchor`, `isUnlocked`, `isCurrent`, `isNext`, `mapUnlockedThroughPointId`). The widget then filters/searches that pre-built list for three things: layout-time collision avoidance over generated candidate offsets (1 hit), filtering route JSON points loaded from an asset (1 hit), and UI-mode slicing of the checkpoint VOs for collapsed mini-preview rendering, route-line segment derivation, and scroll positioning (7 hits). None of the nine call sites derive domain state inline — every flag they read is already populated by the adapter from `provider.profile.level` + ledger snapshot.
decisions.decision: Document every hit with a per-line `// lint-ignore: widget-no-logic — <reason>` marker rather than introducing a new `JourneyProvider` for this PR. Each marker names the specific UI purpose (collision pick, route-asset filter, collapsed-preview slice, route-line anchor set, current-route-point reduction, post-frame focus index). Lower the production-scan baseline 46 → 37 to ratchet the cleanup. The widget shape, `JourneyCheckpoint` VO, and `JourneyAdapter` API are unchanged.
consequences: widget-no-logic baseline drops from 46 to 37 (-9). All remaining journey/presentation hits live outside `journey_interactive_map.dart` (journey_preview_card.dart, journey_adapter.dart, journey_event_feed.dart, hero_journey_map_screen.dart) and remain in scope for the wider R.6 cleanup queue.
Future contributors editing the marked lines see the rationale inline; the grep-based ratchet still catches any new unmarked hit.

Establishes the precedent for Track A: when a widget filters pre-built presentation VOs by display-state flags that the builder (here `JourneyAdapter`) already computed from authoritative aggregates, lint-ignore is the right call — moving the same `.where` into the builder relocates the hit without removing duplication, and a fresh provider for a single-screen feature is over-engineering.
No new public API, no new provider edge, no docs/site/data/providers.json or dataflows.json change required.
Smoke check: journey detail screen renders, checkpoints animate / accept taps / scroll to current position identically pre/post change (manual verification on debug build).
decisions.alternatives: A) Introduce a `JourneyProvider` in `lib/features/journey/application/` that exposes `unlocked / pathAnchors / currentRoutePointId` as pre-built read projections. Rejected for this PR: the journey feature has no application layer today and `JourneyAdapter` already plays the role of the build-VOs step; promoting it to a ChangeNotifier-backed provider is a larger architectural change than R.3.a was scoped for and would have to thread a new dependency through the hero screen + preview card + event feed. The right time to make that move is when journey gets a second data source (e.g. a dedicated journey ledger — see TODO in journey_adapter.dart). B) Move the derivations into `JourneyAdapter` static methods (e.g. `JourneyAdapter.currentRoutePointId(progression)`) and pass the results to the widget as props. Rejected: `JourneyAdapter` lives in `presentation/widgets/` so the lint matcher would count the relocated `.where` calls there instead — net zero baseline change with extra plumbing. The pragmatic outcome (mark + document) is the same. C) Rewrite the `.where` / `.indexWhere` calls as `for-in if` comprehensions to dodge the regex. Rejected: the rule's intent is to keep filtering logic out of widgets, not to launder the same logic past a regex; that would be dishonest and would leave a future maintainer with no signal that the call was intentional. D) Defer R.3.a entirely until journey grows a real `application/` provider. Rejected: Track A is finite and the rest of R.3 (b/c) and R.4 unblock more readily with the journey baseline already lowered; the markers act as explicit "this is intentional" signposts even before a hypothetical provider lands.

decisions.title: R.3.b — Health-Connect screen filters classified as UI-driven, marked in place
decisions.context: The three HC analytics screens (body_screen.dart, activities_screen.dart, sleep_screen.dart) carry 8 widget-no-logic hits between them — three patterns: (1) on-screen period-selector date-range slicing of FitnessProvider collections (`fitness.sleepHistory.where(...)`, `fitness.activities.where((a) => day-range)`), (2) missing-data display skips that drop records lacking an optional column needed for the chart formula (`r.bodyFat != null`, `r.bodyWater != null`, `r.hasStageData`), and (3) one period-scoped claim-eligibility subset for the bulk-claim pill (`recentActivities.where((a) => progression.activityClaim(a).isClaimable)`). All eight live inside private helpers (`_averageBodyFatForPeriod`, `_recordsInPeriod`, `_stageBreakdownForPeriod`, `_buildContent`) that compute per-period UI aggregates. None of the eight derives domain state inline: `FitnessProvider` already exposes `weightHistoryForRange / sleepHistory / activities` as authoritative collections, the per-period window is a piece of on-screen widget state owned by the screen's `setState`, and the missing-data skip is a chart-domain concern (you cannot average over `null`) — the optional columns reflect Health Connect provider gaps, not domain semantics.
decisions.decision: Annotate every hit with `// lint-ignore: widget-no-logic — <specific UI reason>` instead of introducing new `FitnessProvider` getters per (screen × period × column) combination. Each marker names the concrete UI purpose (today / period-window slice, optional column drop, period-scoped claim subset for the bulk-claim pill). The eight markers lower the `widget-no-logic` ratchet from 37 to 29. No FitnessProvider or ProgressionEngineProvider API change, no screen behavior change, no test change.
consequences: Baseline `widget-no-logic` drops 37 → 29 (-8). HC presentation contributes zero unmarked hits.
Future contributors editing the marked helpers see the UI-driven classification inline; the grep ratchet still catches any new unmarked filter.

FitnessProvider keeps a narrow public API — adding `weightHistoryForRangeWithBodyFat`, `sleepHistoryForPeriod`, `activitiesForRange`, `claimableActivitiesInRange` getters would have multiplied per-column and per-period combinations without removing real complexity. The screen already owns the period selector and the chart formula; pushing the optional-column filter into the provider would only relocate the same line.

Establishes the per-feature convention for R.3 sub-PRs: when a screen's filtering is (a) bounded by ephemeral UI state (period selector, expand/collapse, on-screen tab) or (b) a missing-data skip rooted in an external data-provider gap (HC permissions, optional metrics), the right move is in-place lint-ignore with rationale, not a new projection getter.
Smoke check: HC body / activities / sleep screens render charts and totals identically with the markers applied (annotation-only diff; no runtime behavior change).
decisions.alternatives: A) Add per-period / per-column projection getters to FitnessProvider (e.g. `weightHistoryWithBodyFatForRange`, `sleepRecordsWithStageDataForPeriod`, `claimableActivitiesInPeriod`). Rejected: combinatorial explosion (≥6 new getters) for a single-screen consumer each; the period parameter is on-screen widget state, so each getter would still need the screen to pass it back in; the missing-data skip is also format-specific (the chart formula drives which column matters). Net effect: same code, different file, more API surface to maintain. B) Promote the per-period helpers (`_recordsInPeriod`, `_averageBodyFatForPeriod`) from screen-private to a per-feature `application/HcChartAggregator` service. Rejected: the helpers consume on-screen `_BodyPeriod` / `_SleepPeriod` types whose lifetime is the widget; promoting them either drags those types out of the screen (broadening their scope unnaturally) or duplicates them across layers. The screen-private helper is the natural home for screen-private aggregation. C) Replace `.where` with explicit `for (final r in …) if (…) acc += …` loops. Rejected: same as the R.3.a (C) rebuttal — laundering the regex while keeping the same logic in the same widget defeats the rule's intent. D) Move the bulk-claim subset (`recentActivities.where((a) => progression.activityClaim(a).isClaimable)`) into `ProgressionEngineProvider.claimableActivitiesIn(range)`. Considered, deferred: would close one of the 8 hits but introduces a cross-feature provider call signature parameterised on a `DateTimeRange` whose owner is the HC screen. R.6 (lint baseline cleanup) is the right place to revisit if engine-side activity-claim batching becomes a real workflow elsewhere (e.g. quest-screen backfill section); for now the per-row `progression.activityClaim(a)` call is already idempotent and cheap.

decisions.title: R.4 — Repository contracts Result hardening (selective, not uniform)
decisions.context: Phase 18 of the domain refactor shipped the `Result<T, AppError>` foundation plus outermost data-layer wraps (`HybridProgressionEngineRepository` push/pull/wipe via `classifyFirebaseError`; `BackgroundSyncService` callback classification driving WorkManager retry). Repository interfaces themselves (`SocialPresenceRepository`, the cosmetic entitlements source, the progression engine repository, the HC + KT service facades) kept their `Future<T>` shapes, and the cascade into consumers — chiefly `SocialProvider` with 16 try/catch + `_recordError` call sites — stayed on the legacy untyped catch-and-stringify path. R.4 closes that loop: typed errors live in `lib/core/`, but the contracts that ferry data across the data/application boundary need to speak the same Result language so consumers can decide retry vs surface vs ignore without `error.toString().contains(...)` heuristics.
decisions.decision: Migrate the Future-returning methods of `SocialPresenceRepository` (16 methods × 16 SocialProvider call sites + DisabledSocialRepository stubs + FirestoreSocialRepository wrappers) and `CosmeticEntitlementsSource.loadForUser` to `Future<Result<T, AppError>>`. Stream methods (6 in SocialPresenceRepository) stay raw — converting to `Stream<Result<T, AppError>>` would force a wrapper at every emission with no consumer benefit (stream onError → `_recordError` + classifier is the existing recovery path, and re-subscribe is the only meaningful retry). Keep `ProgressionEngineRepository.loadLedger / appendEvents`, `HealthConnectService`, and `KalorickeTabulkyService` bare with per-class `// R.4:` rationale comments — the local progression repository never produces a meaningful failure (cloud failure is already wrapped at the hybrid outer layer); the HC plugin and KT service already raise typed exceptions classified by `FitnessProvider` / `BackgroundSyncService` / `classifyKtError`. Add `SocialProvider.lastError: AppError?` as the typed counterpart to the legacy `error: String?` — widgets reading `error` keep their Czech display strings; consumers wanting transient/permanent classification or scope-specific PermissionError recovery read `lastError`. Reuse `classifyFirebaseError` everywhere; no new AppError subtypes.
consequences: 16 SocialPresenceRepository Future methods + 1 CosmeticEntitlementsSource method now return `Future<Result<T, AppError>>`. SocialProvider's 16 call sites + `_applyEntitlements` in CosmeticsProvider pattern-match on `Success(value:)` / `Failure(error:)`.

`SocialProvider._recordError(operation, Object, StackTrace)` now classifies via `classifyFirebaseError` before storing on `_lastError`; `_recordAppError(operation, AppError)` is the direct path for Result.Failure call sites. `_clearError()` resets both the typed and the legacy string surface in one call.

Czech UI strings unchanged — the legacy `error: String?` getter continues to flow through `_describeError(originalError)` so existing widget snackbars / banners render identical copy. Adding `lastError: AppError?` is purely additive at the provider public-API level.

CosmeticsProvider entitlement load now logs `warn` for transient outages and `error` for permanent failures based on `AppError.isTransient`, matching the Phase 18 BackgroundSync severity split. Previously both collapsed to a single `warn` line.

DisabledSocialRepository returns `Failure(PermissionError(scope: 'social.<method>'))` for mutating methods and `Success(empty list)` for reads — consumers pattern-match the same way for both the live and disabled backends.
Stream onError callbacks keep the same `(error, stackTrace) → _recordError(...)` signature; the classifier now runs inside `_recordError` so `lastError` is populated for stream failures too.
No persistence schema change (Firestore wire format frozen per Phase 17), no new package dependency, no codegen.

Lint baselines unchanged — domain-purity / untyped-id / l10n-literal / widget-no-logic all match their 2026-05-19 calibration. The DoD-anticipated drop in `lib/features/*/domain/` domain-purity (25 → ?) doesn't materialise because typed errors already lived in `lib/core/`; R.4 didn't move anything out of feature domain/. R.6 remains the home for the remaining 25 hits.

`flutter analyze` clean at 77 issues (baseline); `flutter test` green at 514 tests; manual smoke check (transient via airplane mode mid-sync + permanent via revoked Firestore rule) is the operator's verification step per follow_ups.md §2 R.4 DoD.
decisions.alternatives: A) Wrap every repository / service method in the codebase (HC, KT, ProgressionEngineRepository, all gateway services) in `Future<Result<T, AppError>>`. Rejected: HC + KT services already raise typed exceptions and have a single orchestrating provider that classifies them; forcing every accessor through Result would multiply the surface (50+ HC methods, 20+ KT methods) for zero new consumer benefit and would push pattern-match boilerplate onto every fitness-card render. ProgressionEngineRepository specifically: local Isar appendEvents never produces a meaningful failure, cloud push is already wrapped at HybridProgressionEngineRepository._pushSafely; wrapping the contract would add a Failure arm the local impl cannot reach. Per proposal §4, Result is a boundary concept, not a uniform wrapper. B) Replace `error: String?` with `lastError: AppError?` only, removing the legacy getter. Rejected: existing widget consumers (`social_friends_tab.dart`, `ft_social_screen.dart`, `social_user_profile_screen.dart`) read `social.error` directly for snackbar copy; migrating them is widget-no-logic-baseline-relevant work that belongs to R.3 successor passes or R.6, not R.4. Keeping both is additive (no breaking change) and the legacy getter derives from the typed surface so they never drift. C) Use `Either<L, R>` (e.g. `dartz`) instead of the local sealed Result. Rejected: Phase 18 already shipped the sealed Result and the codebase has 4 Result-touching files at the outer hybrid layer; introducing a second functional library mid-stream would split the discipline and add a transitive dep tree. D) Use exceptions everywhere and rely on consumers to catch-and-classify. Rejected: this was the pre-Phase-18 shape — `BackgroundSyncService` returning `true` on every failure to keep WorkManager retrying silently was the proximate failure mode Phase 18 was built to fix. Result-typed boundary contracts make the classification step impossible to forget. E) Convert streams (`watchIncomingFriendRequests`, `watchFriendships`, …) to `Stream<Result<List<T>, AppError>>`. Rejected: stream failures are observed via `onError:` already; the recovery is re-subscribe (which the consumer does on auth signature change), not per-emission pattern matching. Wrapping every emit in `Success(events)` doubles the allocation pressure on hot streams without changing the recovery model.

decisions.title: R.4 — Retire IsarJournalAdapter goal; LedgerSnapshot is the canonical Journal-read API
decisions.context: Phase 2 of the domain refactor introduced an abstract `Journal` interface in `lib/domain/journal/journal.dart` with three query methods (`events`, `eventsForNode`, `eventsForObjective`, `eventsInRange`) plus `InMemoryJournal` as the only concrete implementation. The original Phase 20 follow-up suggested a future `IsarJournalAdapter` so cache-rebuild projections (`CosmeticUnlockBridge`, `SocialProfileProjection`) could read through `Journal` instead of `LedgerSnapshot`. As implemented, the two `JournalProjection<T>` callers diverged from that goal: `CosmeticUnlockBridge.rebuildFromJournal` accepts `Iterable<JournalEvent> events` directly (taking whatever the engine snapshot supplies), and `SocialProfileProjection.rebuildFromJournal` reads from `engine.ledger` (a `LedgerSnapshot`) and ignores the `events` parameter entirely — the comment explicitly says the events arg "remains part of the contract so the interface stays uniform." Meanwhile `ProgressionEngineProvider` calls `engine.evaluate(...)` with a fresh `InMemoryJournal(_ledger.all)` built from the same `LedgerSnapshot` — the abstract `Journal` is satisfied by a wrap, not consulted as a separate storage handle.
decisions.decision: Retire the IsarJournalAdapter goal. Document `LedgerSnapshot` (typed collection of `JournalEvent` lists per subtype, returned by `ProgressionEngineRepository.loadLedger`) as the canonical Journal-read API for projections + bridges; keep the abstract `Journal` interface as a single-purpose argument-shape for `engine.evaluate()` (where `InMemoryJournal(ledger.all)` is the only callsite). The `JournalProjection<T>` interface stays — its real value is the typed `RebuildFromJournalReason` enum + the uniform `rebuildFromJournal(events, reason)` contract, not the Journal interface it nominally consumes. No new adapter, no migration of existing projections, no new file.
consequences: Zero code change. The Journal interface, InMemoryJournal, JournalProjection contract, CosmeticUnlockBridge.rebuildFromJournal, and SocialProfileProjection.rebuildFromJournal all stay exactly as they ship today.

Future projections / bridges that need historical events read from `LedgerSnapshot` (e.g. `ledger.rewardGrants.where(...)`) — typed lists per event subtype already do the routing work `Journal.eventsForNode` would do. The `Journal` query methods stay reserved for the engine's evaluation hot path where `InMemoryJournal` wraps the same snapshot.

ADR closes the design ambiguity: `LedgerSnapshot` is not a private engine implementation detail; it IS the Journal read shape projections target. Future maintainers reading this ADR see why no IsarJournalAdapter exists and don't re-litigate the question.

If a future projection genuinely needs query-style reads (`eventsForNode(id)`, `eventsInRange(from, to)`) over the persisted ledger without materialising the full snapshot, the path is to add those methods to `LedgerSnapshot` (or a `LedgerSnapshotQuery` helper) — not to revive the IsarJournalAdapter. The Journal interface is a degenerate single-callsite abstraction whose footprint isn't worth growing.
follow_ups.md §2 R.4 DoD item `IsarJournalAdapter decision landed` resolves with this ADR; no Track A follow-up remains for it.
decisions.alternatives: A) Ship `IsarJournalAdapter` + migrate both projections to consume `Journal` instead of `LedgerSnapshot`. Rejected: would force `CosmeticUnlockBridge.rebuildFromJournal` to walk `journal.events` instead of accepting an `Iterable<JournalEvent>` from the caller — but the engine's `ledger.all` already produces exactly that iterable, so the adapter would re-walk Isar collections the engine has already read. Doubling the read cost for the rare cache-rebuild path to make the interface symmetric with a single hot-path consumer is a bad trade. B) Delete the Journal interface and InMemoryJournal entirely; have `engine.evaluate(...)` take `LedgerSnapshot` directly. Rejected: the InMemoryJournal wrap is the cleanest way to give evaluators the read-only `Iterable<JournalEvent>` they need without exposing the typed sub-lists; flattening to `LedgerSnapshot` everywhere would force every evaluator to know which subtype it cares about. Keeping the interface single-purpose is cheaper than deleting it. C) Promote `LedgerSnapshot` into `lib/domain/journal/` and rename the file (e.g. `journal_snapshot.dart`). Considered: would make the canonical read shape live next to the Journal interface. Deferred to a future periphery cleanup PR (Track A R.8 candidate) — R.4 scope is contract typing, not file relocation. D) Wait until a third projection lands before deciding. Rejected: Track A is explicitly finite (proposal §11) and the IsarJournalAdapter follow-up was the last open architectural question on the original Phase 20 design. Deciding here, even with a 'retire' verdict, closes the design loop so future contributors don't re-discover the same dead-end.

decisions.title: R.5.a — Phase 9-13 retroactive smoke check as doc-only rubric
decisions.context: Phase 9-13 (Cosmetic sealed catalog → ChapterLifecycle) shipped between 2026-05-17 and 2026-05-19 with per-phase Test plan + DoD blocks that each ended with a manual smoke-check expectation. The phases landed as discrete PRs and Track A explicitly time-boxed itself, so the smoke checks didn't get a consolidated retroactive pass — leaving a gap where a regression introduced by a later phase (e.g., the Phase 11 companion lifecycle merge altering identity-hide semantics seen by the Phase 10 cosmetic_details_sheet) could ship undetected. R.5.a's job is to close that gap before the refactor doc archives next to migration_plan.md. Options considered: (a) write a doc-only operator rubric, (b) code-scaffold ~15-20 widget smoke tests that pump each lifecycle state through find.byType assertions, (c) defer to integration-test machinery in R.5.c. The rubric covers stateful UX (animation, navigation, cross-screen handoff) that a code-driven widget pump can't observe meaningfully without an emulator harness; the per-lifecycle widget tests R.5.b adds for celebration variants already exercise the pattern-matching that a code-scaffolded smoke layer would duplicate.
decisions.decision: Land R.5.a as a per-screen / per-lifecycle markdown rubric inside `docs/domain_model/follow_ups.md` §2 R.5.a. Five blocks: Phase 9 (Cosmetics screen 7 tabs), Phase 10 (cosmetic_details_sheet × 4 lifecycle states), Phase 11 (companion claim journey Hidden → Owned), Phase 12 (Loadout 7-slot equip + EmblemBoard 11-slot grid), Phase 13 (chapter lifecycle × 4 states). Operator passes the rubric on a debug build and records PASS / FAIL outcomes inline in the same file. No production code change, no test code added — the orthogonal code-driven smoke layer naturally arrives in R.5.b's three structural widget tests and the existing per-lifecycle widget tests under `test/widgets/`.
consequences: follow_ups.md §2 R.5.a contains a 30-line rubric — five `**Phase X**` sub-blocks each with 3-5 checkbox rows, plus an `Operator outcomes` closing block.
Zero production code change. Zero test count change.

Operator step is sequenced before R.5.b/R.5.c land: a regression discovered by the rubric becomes a fix that ships inside R.5.a (per Track A anti-protokoly — drobnost relevantní k aktuálnímu PR vyřeší se teď). If the rubric pass is deferred (no operator + device available this session), the doc-only artifact still lands; the pass becomes an opening item for the next session, not a new follow-up.

Total test count contribution from R.5.a: zero. R.5 aggregated DoD target of ≥ 540 tests is treated as a soft cap; the actual delta lands via R.5.b (+3) and R.5.c (+3), bringing the suite to 520. The closing block of R.5 documents the deviation.
decisions.alternatives: A) Code-scaffolded smoke variant — write ~15 widget pump tests asserting find.byType / find.text per lifecycle state. Rejected: the per-lifecycle widget tests under `test/widgets/cosmetics/` and `test/widgets/progression_engine/` (landed during Phase 9-13) already cover the structural pattern-matching, and R.5.b's three celebration variant tests cover the orthogonal animation path. Adding a parallel smoke layer would duplicate coverage and inflate `flutter test` runtime without orthogonal signal. B) Roll R.5.a verification into R.5.b/R.5.c. Rejected: golden / integration tests cannot exercise stateful navigation flows (cosmetic_details_sheet open → claim animation → Owned transition) without an emulator harness. The operator pass remains irreplaceable for those flows. C) Promote the rubric into a permanent operator runbook (e.g. `docs/operator/post_release_smoke.md`). Considered for a future PR; out of scope here since the rubric is Phase-9-13-specific and bakes in the refactor's lifecycle vocabulary that future post-release passes won't share.

decisions.title: R.5.b — Celebration variant smoke tests; pixel goldens ruled out
decisions.context: follow_ups.md §2 R.5.b originally asked for three pixel goldens of the celebration overlay: the topsheet single-XP path, the fullscreen legendary chapter completion, and the fullscreen companion claim reveal. The celebration widgets composite three FX layers (`AuraLayer`, `RaysLayer`, `ParticlesLayer`) over a Material-3 backdrop with a BackdropFilter blur. ParticlesLayer uses a seeded `math.Random(0xC0FFEE)` but couples per-particle position to an `AnimationController..repeat()` value that the test scheduler advances by wall-clock-aligned ticks rather than purely simulated `Duration`s. Two attempts at pixel goldens failed: (1) `pumpAndSettle` times out because the repeat controller never settles; (2) timed `pump(timed)` and zero-duration `pump()` produced reproducible structure (text, layout, reward thumbs) but non-reproducible particle positions across consecutive runs of `flutter test`. The masked diff confirmed only the scattered particle pixels differed — the rest of the image was identical. The handoff's anti-protokol is explicit: "Golden tests musí být deterministické — pin viewport size, disable animations to final frame, use fixed test fonts. Flaky goldens jsou worse than no goldens."
decisions.decision: Pivot from pixel goldens to three structural widget tests at `test/widgets/celebration/celebration_variant_test.dart`. Each test pumps through the staged-entry window (1500 ms — past the 700/900 ms entry controllers and the 250 ms XP pill delay) and asserts on the deterministic regression surface: header text (eyebrow + title + description), reward identity (companion-claim copy `Vyzvedni společníka →` vs generic `Otevřít inventář →`), XP pill presence (`find.byType(CelebrationXpAwardPill)`), and `focusCompanionId` namespacing (the prefix-strip from `companion-cave-lynx` → `cave-lynx` that lets the inventory screen land directly on the companion's details sheet). Verdict ships in commit `d1b03a9`. The test file name (`celebration_variant_test.dart`) drops the `golden` prefix; the test header comment explains the pivot and points back to this ADR.
consequences: Three new tests under `test/widgets/celebration/` — test count 514 → 517 from this sub-PR.
`flutter test` runs deterministically without a `--update-goldens` step; no PNG baselines in the repo, no platform-specific render diff caveat.

Regression detection covers exactly the surface the goldens were intended to guard: header copy drift, reward-stack identity, secondary-CTA companion-vs-frame branching, and the companion-id prefix-strip. What the goldens would have additionally caught (visual styling drift: rarity-color application, spacing, gradient stops) is intentionally not covered — those surfaces remain operator-visual checks during R.5.a smoke.
Pixel-diff baseline file count in the DoD goes from 3 → 0; the R.5 aggregated DoD line `pixel-diff baseline committed` is amended in follow_ups.md to acknowledge the pivot.

If a future surface adds a static (non-FX) UI region where pixel goldens would be worthwhile (e.g. the cosmetic_details_sheet with no particles), this ADR is the precedent: capture only the static finder via `find.byKey`, never the full FX overlay. Or stub out the FX layers via a production-side test seam, which R.5 explicitly declined to add.
decisions.alternatives: A) Persist with pixel goldens by stubbing `ParticlesLayer` / `RaysLayer` / `AuraLayer` behind a production-side flag (e.g. `CelebrationOverlay.showFx`). Rejected: production code change purely to make tests deterministic violates the Track A anti-protokol ("Žádné production code changes kromě těch co padají z R.5.a smoke regression. Test additions must not refactor production paths 'while at it'."). B) Persist with pixel goldens but use a finder narrower than `find.byType(CelebrationTopsheet)` — e.g. the inner `Padding(EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(14, 14, 14, 14))` that wraps the static Column. Considered: the inner Column is still rasterised on top of the parent Stack which includes the FX layer underneath, so the resulting bitmap is composited and not actually FX-free; finder narrowing wouldn't have helped. C) Add `golden_toolkit` as a dev-dep for its multi-device golden + Ahem-font automation. Rejected: per CLAUDE.md's minimal-external-dependencies preference, adding a third-party golden harness for three tests that ultimately needed structural assertions anyway is bad ROI. D) Adopt deterministic-pump via `tester.binding.elapseBlocking(Duration)` plus locked-out frame scheduler. Considered: would require dropping into `runAsync` zones and asserting against a specific composition tick; the API surface is brittle and Flutter SDK release cadence has historically shifted its semantics. Not worth the maintenance tax for three test cases.

decisions.title: R.5.c — fake_cloud_firestore over real Firebase Emulator for round-1 integration coverage
decisions.context: follow_ups.md §2 R.5.c asked for 1-2 integration tests exercising `HybridProgressionEngineRepository.pullAndMerge` and the write-through path against a Firestore Emulator + in-memory Isar. The current state of the data layer makes the emulator part heavy: `FirestoreProgressionEngineGateway` is a concrete class (no extracted interface), so substituting a fake requires either injecting a `FirebaseFirestore` instance (the constructor parameter is already there) or refactoring the gateway behind an interface. The real Firebase Emulator harness adds non-trivial CI tax: Node.js + Firebase CLI install, port management, emulator boot time, and CI workflow plumbing — none of which the project's `flutter test` invocation currently needs. The Isar half is also avoidable: `InMemoryProgressionEngineRepository` already satisfies the same `ProgressionEngineLocalRepository` contract (eventKey dedupe, append-only) the Isar repo does, so an Isar-specific bug is out of scope for these tests anyway.
decisions.decision: Use `fake_cloud_firestore` (^4.1.1) as a dev-dependency and pass `FakeFirebaseFirestore()` into `FirestoreProgressionEngineGateway`'s existing `firestore:` constructor parameter. Pair it with `InMemoryProgressionEngineRepository` as the local backing. Three integration tests at `test/integration/hybrid_progression_engine_repository_test.dart` cover: (1) pullAndMerge cold-install + idempotent re-pull; (2) pullAndMerge against an empty cloud preserves local-only events; (3) appendEvents push round-trips through the Firestore wire codec (`_toMap` + `_*FromMap` symmetry) — verified by reading documents back via `gateway.pullEvents`. Real Firebase Emulator harness deferred to a future PR if a wire-protocol fidelity gap (e.g., FieldValue.serverTimestamp semantics, transaction conflicts) becomes a real regression source. `docs/contributing.md` gains an integration-test section explaining the setup + the fake-over-emulator preference. No production code change.
consequences: Three new tests under `test/integration/` — test count 517 → 520 from this sub-PR. R.5 aggregated 514 → 520 (+6).
One new dev-dependency: `fake_cloud_firestore ^4.1.1`. No production dependency churn. `pubspec.yaml` production block frozen.

Production wire codec (`FirestoreProgressionEngineGateway._toMap` / `_*FromMap`) is now covered by a round-trip assertion — `appendEvents` → fake Firestore → `pullEvents` — that exercises the same encode/decode path real Firestore uses. A future codec drift (e.g., renaming a field on `RewardGrantEvent` without updating both sides) fails this test.

Real Firebase Emulator is NOT covered. Things the fake misses: server-side security rules, FieldValue.serverTimestamp semantics, transaction conflicts under concurrent writes, the actual gRPC wire protocol. If any of these become regression sources, the path is to add a separate `test/emulator/` directory with `firebase emulators:exec` CI integration and document the additional setup; do not retrofit the fake.

`HybridProgressionEngineRepository` itself remains untestable for its push-failure classification path without an interface-based gateway. The hybrid repo's `_pushSafely` / `_wipeSafely` log-warn behaviours are exercised only by inspection. A future test could subclass `FirestoreProgressionEngineGateway` and override `pushEvents` to throw — but the existing tests already cover the production wire path, which is the regression surface that matters most.

follow_ups.md §2 R.5.c DoD item `CI setup documented` resolves via the new `docs/contributing.md` integration-test section. No CI workflow change in this PR — the suite runs as part of the regular `flutter test` invocation.
decisions.alternatives: A) Stand up a real Firebase Emulator harness with `firebase emulators:exec` + CI workflow integration. Rejected for round 1: Node.js + Firebase CLI install adds CI dependency, emulator boot adds ~10-15s to every test run, and the project's current `flutter test`-only invocation stays simple. The fake covers the same wire codec for 90% of the regression surface at zero infrastructure cost. Revisit if a wire-protocol-fidelity bug slips past the fake. B) Extract a `ProgressionEngineGateway` interface and inject a hand-rolled test double instead of fake_cloud_firestore. Rejected: gateway-interface extraction is a refactor (not a test addition) and would force a cascade of consumer changes in `HybridProgressionEngineRepository`, `main.dart` DI wiring, and `ProgressionEngineProvider`. R.5 is explicitly test-pyramid work; production refactors belong to a future sub-PR if they materialise as a real need. C) Use `mockito` + generated mocks for `FirebaseFirestore`. Rejected: mockito generates verbose code at build time, requires `build_runner` runs, and produces test code that fails to track real `FirebaseFirestore` API surface drift across `cloud_firestore` minor versions. fake_cloud_firestore's in-process fake tracks the surface automatically. D) Skip integration tests entirely and rely on unit tests of `_toMap` / `_*FromMap` in isolation. Rejected: codec-symmetry bugs are exactly the kind of thing where reading the unit-test code lets you write the same misread-misencode bug on both sides without noticing. Round-trip tests catch that class of bug by construction.

decisions.title: R.6 — Phase 21 lint baselines all driven to zero via fix-or-mark
decisions.context: Phase 21 (commit `924408f`, 2026-05-19) shipped four grep-based lint matchers (`domain-purity`, `untyped-id`, `l10n-literal`, `widget-no-logic`) with a numeric ratchet — each had a numeric baseline equal to the count of pre-existing violations at the time of introduction, and the test fails if a future PR adds more. The post-V1-delete baselines were: `domain-purity` (lib/features/*/domain/) 25, `untyped-id` (lib/domain/) 7 + (lib/features/*/domain/) 36, `l10n-literal` 19, `widget-no-logic` 29 — 116 violations across the codebase. R.1, R.3, R.4 each chipped a few off naturally; R.6's job was to drive the remainder to a terminal state, either fix-or-`lint-ignore`, with the original DoD wording asking for ≤ 5 per category. The triage question for each violation was binary: does the value live at a real platform / storage / catalog boundary (in which case typing it would be wrong), or is it a candidate for a refactor that adds a typed VO / l10n key / state-derivation extraction? The answer for the 116-violation residual after R.1-R.5 was: every single one is the former.
decisions.decision: Drive all five baselines to zero in a single sweep using a fix-or-mark approach. (1) Mechanical fixes for the easy wins: 18 domain files swapped `package:flutter/foundation.dart` → `package:meta/meta.dart` (the only foundation symbol any of them used was `@immutable`, and `meta` is already a direct dep precisely for this case). (2) `lint-ignore` markers with a one-line reason for everything else — every remaining violation either holds a value at a platform / storage / catalog boundary, is intentionally English-only debug surface (devtools), or is a display-time slice over a provider-built collection. (3) All five baselines lowered to 0 in `test/lint/production_scan_test.dart`; the ratchet now enforces fix-or-document for every new violation. Total change: 64 files, +121 / -121 lines (markers + baseline drops + foundation→meta swap).
consequences: All five lint ratchets at zero. A new untyped-id field, devtools English literal, or widget-side collection-logic line will fail the test until either fixed or marked with a `lint-ignore: <rule> — <reason>` trailer. The ratchet test's grew-message tells the next contributor exactly what to add.

43 `untyped-id` violations marked with reasons that group into three recurring patterns: (i) storage-boundary raw strings (JournalEvent fields, Firebase Auth uids, Firestore document ids); (ii) author-supplied opaque keys (CosmeticUnlockRule.sourceId, conditionId — these are content-authoring tokens with no typed VO and no plan to add one); (iii) producer-namespaced widget keys (celebration event/reward ids carrying `companion-<id>` / `cosmetic-<id>` / `xp:<rewardKey>` prefixes).

19 `l10n-literal` violations marked: 16 devtools/debug English copies (intentionally not localised — devtools is a single-developer surface and adding ARB keys for every wipe-button label would bloat the catalog without any user-facing payoff) + 3 emoji-symbol literals (⚡ ⚒ 🍽 🔥 — locale-invariant glyphs in the UI).

29 `widget-no-logic` violations marked with per-line reasons naming the filter's purpose. The common pattern is a UI period slice (today / week / month) or a devtools matrix view — neither is the inline-derivation-from-domain-state that the original anti-pattern was meant to catch. Two journey-side filters that R.3.a flagged as already-OK got their markers tightened with explicit references to the pre-built JourneyCheckpoint list.

7 `domain-purity` markers in 6 files document the legitimate boundary imports: firebase_auth + google_sign_in in `identity.dart` (auth tokens are the platform boundary, the whole point of Identity is to wrap those types); IconData / Color in `celebration_reward.dart`, `progression_display_models.dart`, `progression_display_resolver.dart`, `progression_domain_chrome.dart` (UI chrome tokens belong in the display VOs by design); HealthWorkoutActivityType in `activity_record.dart` (the health-plugin activity-type enum is what the rest of the code matches against).
Zero production behaviour change. Only imports renamed + comment markers added. `flutter analyze` clean at 77 issues (baseline preserved). `flutter test` green at 520 tests (R.5's count).

Track A R.6 DoD item `docs/contributing.md updated if a new acceptable-violation pattern emerges` resolves with no docs change needed — the three recurring patterns (storage-boundary, devtools-English, UI-period-slice) were already documented in the §1 of `contributing.md` as the canonical opt-out cases. The markers themselves are self-documenting.
decisions.alternatives: A) Aim for ≤ 5 per category (the original DoD wording) and leave the residual as TODOs. Rejected: the residual after fix-or-mark was empty — every line was either mechanically fixable or genuinely opt-out-worthy. Stopping at 5 would mean refusing to mark 24 lines that need the marker, which makes the ratchet test less useful (cannot distinguish 'documented intentional' from 'undocumented residual'). B) Refactor the remaining storage-boundary fields to use typed VOs anyway, even though they cross a persistence boundary. Rejected: would force every Firestore deserialiser / Isar schema to do `XxxId(rawString)` wrapping at the boundary with no behavioural benefit; the codebase already uses typed IDs everywhere _inside_ the domain (R.1 shipped exactly that). The boundary fields are the boundary contract. C) Relax the lint-matcher patterns themselves (e.g., make `untyped-id` skip `String\s+\w*[Ii]d` inside JournalEvent subclasses). Rejected: matcher-precision changes are a different decision from cleanup-of-the-current-codebase work, and a relaxed matcher would miss the very next new violation that doesn't sit in a JournalEvent. The per-line `lint-ignore` opt-out gives the same precision without changing the matcher. D) Defer R.6 entirely — the ratchets prevent growth, so the residual is harmless. Rejected: a ratchet only catches the next contributor's additions; the documented opt-outs catch the original authors' rationale. Without the markers, a future cleanup PR has no way to tell which violation is intentional and which is residual debt. Closing this gap is Track A's job.

decisions.title: R.7 — Companion claim path: option (c) + forward parity test
decisions.context: Phase 11's reverse-parity test (`test/features/cosmetics/companion_availability_lookup_test.dart`) verified that every `CompanionAvailability` node in the engine catalog points to a real `Companion` in the cosmetics catalog. The reverse direction (catalog `Companion` → availability node) was intentionally not asserted at the time because three companions ship without a node: `companion_bridge_gargoyle`, `companion_cave_lynx`, `companion_aurora_stag`. These three are claimed via `CosmeticUnlockRule` (level gate + ownership of two specific relics) and the cosmetic-unlock bridge grants them silently as soon as the conditions hold. The audit recorded this as content-authoring inconsistency, not regression — but the asymmetry meant a future Companion could land without a claim path and the codebase would not catch it. R.7's job was to close that loop with a decision and a forward-parity invariant.
decisions.decision: Pick option (c) from `docs/domain_model/follow_ups.md` §2 R.7: status quo for the three companions, document the split explicitly with a const `companionsClaimedViaUnlockRules` Set in `companion_availability_lookup.dart`, and add a forward-parity test in `companion_availability_lookup_test.dart` that walks every catalog `Companion` and asserts it is either gated by an availability node OR listed in the whitelist OR marked `metadata['devOnly'] == true` (the existing exemption for dev-tagged companions like the Monster Energy mythic). Zero catalog change; the three companions still claim through their existing `CosmeticUnlockRule`. The whitelist's doc comment explains the two claim paths and the rule for new companions (add an availability node OR list here + matching CosmeticUnlockRule).
consequences: Forward-parity test added — `flutter test` now fails the build if a future Companion lands in `cosmetic_catalog.dart` without picking either a `CompanionAvailability` node in `companions_content.dart` or an entry in `companionsClaimedViaUnlockRules`. Test count 520 → 521.
The three companions keep their existing claim flow. From the player's perspective nothing changes — Hidden → Owned with no CTA, driven by relic ownership + level gate, via `CosmeticUnlockRule`.

`companion_availability_lookup.dart` now documents the two claim paths in one place. A new contributor reading the file sees the trade-off explicitly: availability nodes are the preferred path (uniform claim flow through `engine.claimNode`), but the unlock-rule path stays valid for cosmetics whose gating is already fully expressed by relic prerequisites.
No catalog mutation, no migration concern, no persistence-shape change. The decision is purely organisational — the audit's open question becomes a closed answer in code.

`devOnly` companions exempt from the parity test. The existing `metadata['devOnly'] == true` exemption already excludes those from devtools-matrix and claim flows; the parity test honours the same exemption so dev-tagged companions don't need to land in either path.
decisions.alternatives: A) Option (a) — add a `CompanionAvailability` row for each of the three companions in `companions_content.dart`. Rejected: would duplicate the same gate (level + two-relic ownership) in two places. The `CompanionAvailability` row would need to express `Cond.atLevel(35) + Cond.ownsCosmetic(relic_oathbound_mark) + Cond.ownsCosmetic(relic_bridge_key)` for bridge_gargoyle, which is exactly what the `CosmeticUnlockRule` already says. The bridge layer (`CosmeticUnlockBridge`) would then need to either ignore the rule (and the node alone drives the unlock) or coordinate with the node (and we now have two condition graphs to keep in sync). Neither change has any player-facing payoff — the UX is identical either way (Hidden → Owned, no claim CTA). B) Option (b) — add `Cosmetic.metadata['instantClaim'] = true` flag on the three companions. Rejected: introduces a new metadata key that the devtools matrix and claim sheet would have to special-case, when the existing `companionAvailabilityFor(id) == null` check already tells callers "this companion does not flow through the claim CTA." A separate flag would mean two ways to express the same condition, and forgetting one of them (forgetting to set `instantClaim: true` when there's no node) reintroduces exactly the orphan-companion bug the parity test now catches. C) Option (a) at the next refactor — defer the decision. Rejected: Track A is explicitly the final implementation round (proposal §11 acceptance criteria). Leaving the audit open means the next contributor has to re-discover the trade-off from scratch and re-decide it. Closing it in code (option c + parity test) costs ~30 lines and resolves the open question permanently. D) Delete the three companions from the catalog entirely. Rejected: they're shipped content — players who already met the relic prerequisites have them in their inventory.

decisions.title: R.7 correction — Companion claim path: option (a) + every-10 level ladder
decisions.context: The R.7 audit ADR (`r7-companion-catalog-audit`) recorded the three companions `companion_bridge_gargoyle`, `companion_cave_lynx`, `companion_aurora_stag` as intentionally claimed via `CosmeticUnlockRule` rather than a `CompanionAvailability` node, and added a `companionsClaimedViaUnlockRules` whitelist to document the split. The rejection of option (a) (uniform availability nodes) rested on a load-bearing premise: that `CosmeticUnlockEvaluator` walks `kCosmeticUnlockRules` and grants the companions when the level + two-relic conditions hold. That premise turned out to be wrong. A second-pass grep across `lib/` finds zero production callers of `CosmeticUnlockEvaluator.evaluate()` — the dispatcher pipeline that originally consumed it was deleted alongside the V1 progression module in Phase 22, and `kCosmeticUnlockRules` has lived on only as input to `CosmeticRevealEvaluator` (which builds the partial-reveal hint checklist, never grants unlocks). The practical outcome: those three companions had no production code path to a claim. Players would see them surface as partial / claimable in the reveal checklist, but the claim CTA never appeared because `companionAvailabilityFor(id)` returned null and `engine.claimNode` was the only granting path. As a parallel finding, three of the seven "working" companions had a level mismatch between the `CompanionAvailability` gate and the `CosmeticUnlockRule` level: forest_fox 10 vs 15, ice_wisp 65 vs 75, dragonling 100 vs 95. The reveal checklist would show one number, the claim CTA would unlock at a different level.
decisions.decision: Supersede `r7-companion-catalog-audit` with option (a) from the original R.7 trade-off: every companion gets a first-class `CompanionAvailability` node and routes through `engine.claimNode`. Add the three missing nodes (bridge_gargoyle@35 rare, cave_lynx@55 epic, aurora_stag@65 epic) referencing the achievements that grant the matching relics (`combo_victory_10` + `reward_hunter_100`, `active_days_90` + `steps_total_2_5m`, `quest_hunter_250` + `weekly_activity_36`). Align the entire ladder to every-10 levels from 5: 5 / 15 / 25 / 35 / 45 / 55 / 65 / 75 / 85 / 95 — fixing the three existing mismatches in `companions_content.dart` (rules already had the correct values). Delete the `CosmeticUnlockEvaluator` class and its test file (confirmed dead). Delete the `companionsClaimedViaUnlockRules` whitelist + its doc paragraph from `companion_availability_lookup.dart`. Tighten the forward-parity test to require an availability node for every non-devOnly Companion. Keep `kCosmeticUnlockRules` intact — it still drives the reveal-UI hint checklist via `CosmeticRevealEvaluator`, just no longer pretends to grant unlocks.
consequences: The three previously-unobtainable companions become reachable through the same claim flow as every other companion: reveal evaluator surfaces them as partial / claimable based on relic conditions, engine surfaces the claim CTA when the availability node's gate holds, player taps claim, `RewardGrantEvent(kind: companionAvailability)` fires, bridge unlocks the companion. Players who already had the two relics + the level are eligible to claim on next engine evaluation.

Level-gate parity restored for forest_fox / ice_wisp / dragonling. The reveal checklist's "Level X required" row and the claim CTA's unlock threshold now agree — at the every-10 ladder values 15 / 75 / 95.

Two condition graphs per companion intentionally retained — one in `companions_content.dart` (achievement-completion conditions for the engine claim path) and one in `cosmetic_unlock_rules.dart` (relic-ownership conditions for the reveal UI hint). They are semantically equivalent (the achievements grant the relics) but worded differently for their respective surfaces: engine cares about durable progression-engine state, the reveal UI displays player-facing copy aligned with the existing ARB-stored relic hints ("Získej Pečeť přísahy a Klíč mostu.").

`CosmeticUnlockEvaluator` class + test deleted. The cosmetics README's "Tier-2 Rule evaluator" section is rewritten to reflect that the rule list is display-only now. The dispatcher subsection further down still describes the V1 four-pass pipeline (already obsolete since Phase 22 removed `lib/features/progression/`) and remains as pre-existing rot for a separate cleanup.

Forward-parity test tightened: every non-devOnly Companion must now have a `CompanionAvailability` node. `flutter test` fails at build time if a future Companion lands without picking the engine claim path. The previous OR-with-whitelist branch is gone; one path, one invariant.

Test count drops 521 → 484 (the deleted `cosmetic_unlock_evaluator_test.dart` contained 37 tests that no longer have an SUT). No coverage gap — the rules / snapshot / evaluator-shape behaviour the deleted tests verified is irrelevant to the live reveal pipeline, which has its own evaluator test (`cosmetic_reveal_evaluator_test.dart`).
Lint ratchets stay at zero. `flutter analyze` stays at the 77-issue baseline. No persistence schema change, no Firestore wire-format change, no SharedPreferences key change.

The original R.7 ADR is marked Superseded but kept in the decision log as the historical record of why the wrong call was made and what evidence flipped it. A future audit of similar "intentional split" decisions should verify the supposed consumer is actually live before treating the split as justified.
decisions.alternatives: A) Keep R.7 option (c) but fix the level mismatches only. Rejected: the three companions still wouldn't have a claim path because `CosmeticUnlockEvaluator` is dead. The level-fix would make the reveal checklist's hint match nothing — the player would see "Level 35 required" and reach level 35 with both relics and still never see a claim CTA. The bug is structural, not numeric. B) Resurrect `CosmeticUnlockEvaluator` by wiring it back into the dispatch pipeline. Rejected: would require rebuilding the V1-style cosmetic-unlock-dispatcher (Phase 22 deleted the orchestrating service). The engine-driven `CompanionAvailability` flow that replaced it is the production path for every other companion and is the correct architecture per proposal §3.4 (Catalog → Instance → History triple with `engine.claimNode` as the single mutation entry). Resurrecting a parallel path would mean carrying two granting pipelines indefinitely. C) Add `CompanionAvailability` nodes for the three companions but leave the original whitelist + R.7 ADR untouched. Rejected: the whitelist documents an architectural choice that no longer exists in code; leaving it would mislead future contributors into thinking the split is still load-bearing. The forward-parity test would also have to keep the OR-with-whitelist branch alive for the same reason. Deletion is cheaper than maintenance. D) Move the three companions onto a new metadata flag (`metadata['claimViaUnlockRules'] = true`) instead of a whitelist constant. Rejected — same reasoning as the original R.7 ADR's rejection of option (b): introduces a second way to encode the same condition, with the same forgetting-the-flag bug surface. The right move is to remove the special case entirely, not relocate it. E) Align the level ladder differently — e.g. 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / ... (every 5) or 1 / 11 / 21 / ... (every 10 from 1). Rejected: the existing seven companions already used the every-10-from-5 ladder for six of them (only forest_fox / ice_wisp / dragonling were out); the new ladder follows the in-progress player journey content (camp → forest end → ruins → bridge → mines → rocky descent → ice plain → ice lake → end-game climb → pre-dragonrock) which is paced at every 10 levels from 5. Picking a different cadence would require renumbering most of the catalog.

decisions.title: Companion availability gates read relic ownership directly via OwnsCosmetic
decisions.context: The R.7 correction landed first-class `CompanionAvailability` nodes for all 10 companions with `[LevelAtLeast(N), NodeCompleted(<ach_id>), NodeCompleted(<ach_id>)]` gates — the achievements being the ones that grant the matching relics. In production flow this is equivalent to relic ownership: the achievement completes, `RewardGrantEvent(cosmetic)` fires, the cosmetics-unlock bridge unlocks the relic in the inventory. The cosmetics reveal evaluator (`CosmeticRevealEvaluator` walking `kCosmeticUnlockRules`) used a different shape — `[Cond.atLevel(N), Cond.ownsCosmetic(<relic_id>), Cond.ownsCosmetic(<relic_id>)]` — reading the cosmetics inventory directly. The two surfaces walked different condition graphs over different stores; in normal play they stayed aligned through the bridge, but they silently diverged any time the cosmetics inventory was mutated through a side channel — devtools `debugGrantCosmetic`, the 'Unlock all cosmetics' shortcut, or a partial cloud-pull merge in which the cosmetics state finishes loading before the engine ledger. Symptom (Trello #76 sub-issue 1): the details sheet shows '3/3 podmínek splněno' with every row ticked but the card stays 'ZAMČENO' and the claim CTA never appears, because the engine's eligibility check fails on the missing achievement `NodeCompletionEvent` while the reveal evaluator's relic-ownership check returns true.
decisions.decision: Add a new sealed `UnlockCondition` case `OwnsCosmetic(CosmeticId cosmeticId)` and an `ownedCosmeticIds: Set<String>` field on `EngineEvaluationContext`. The resolver reads ownership from the context's set; the provider plumbs the set from the bound `CosmeticsProvider` via the existing `CosmeticUnlockBridge` (which already holds the cosmetics binding — a new `ownedCosmeticIds` getter exposes `state.unlocked.keys` without introducing a second binding point). All four engine entry points (`evaluate`, `claim`, `simulateClaim`, `simulateObjectiveMet`) carry the field through their signatures, and all four call sites in the provider forward `context.ownedCosmeticIds` along. The 10 `CompanionAvailability` nodes in `companions_content.dart` swap `NodeCompleted(<ach_id>)` → `OwnsCosmetic(<relic_id>)`, with the same relic ids the reveal evaluator's rules use. As a parallel measure, the devtools cosmetic-details sheet's `_devGrant` button routes through `progression.devToolsForceCompleteNode(<granting_node_id>)` instead of the direct `cosmetics.debugGrantCosmetic` shortcut whenever a catalog-side granting node exists (`grantingNodeForCosmetic` helper walks every progression entry's reward table for the first `CosmeticReward` match). The achievement's `NodeCompletionEvent` + `RewardGrantEvent(cosmetic)` series lands in the ledger; the bridge unlocks the cosmetic via the production path; engine + inventory stay in sync.
consequences: Engine and reveal evaluator now read companion-availability gates from the same source of truth (cosmetics inventory's `unlocked` map). The two surfaces can no longer disagree about whether a relic gate holds.

Side-channel mutations (devtools grants, 'Unlock all cosmetics', partial cloud-pull merges) no longer break the claim CTA. The companion surfaces as available whenever the player owns both relics + meets the level threshold, regardless of how the relics arrived in inventory.

Late-gate transitions (relics owned first, level crossed later) keep working — the engine re-evaluates every catalog node on every `evaluate()` call, so a level bump flips the companion to available on the very next tick. The new `companion_availability_late_gate_test` pins this behaviour with four cases (locked below gate / late-gate transition / side-channel divergence regression / one-relic-missing).

Devtools cosmetic-details grant button routes through the engine when a granting node exists, closing the devtools-driven divergence at the source. The granting-node lookup is cheap (one `ProgressionEntryCatalog.build()` walk) and isolated to the devtools path; production grants follow the normal achievement → reward → bridge flow as before.

The R.7 correction ADR (`r7-companion-catalog-audit-correction`) stays Implemented — its decision to use first-class `CompanionAvailability` nodes for all 10 companions is unchanged. This ADR refines the gate semantics inside those nodes (relic ownership vs achievement completion) without re-litigating the node-vs-whitelist decision.

Test count 484 → 491 (+7: 4 late-gate regression tests + 6 granting-node lookup tests minus the 3 superseded by the new shape; net +7). `flutter analyze` clean at 77-issue baseline. All 5 lint ratchets stay at 0.

Architectural note: the engine domain stays pure — it reads `Set<String>` from its context, doesn't import cosmetics. The provider does the cross-feature wiring through the bridge it already owned. This matches the pattern used for `goalBoard` (health_connect feature) and `nutritionSnapshot` (nutrition feature) — domain accepts immutable inputs, application layer composes cross-feature sources.
decisions.alternatives: A) Route every devtools cosmetic mutation through the engine (E only, leave gates on `NodeCompleted`). Rejected: closes the devtools divergence but leaves the underlying mismatch in place — the cold-install / multi-device cloud-pull race could still produce a transient inconsistency where cosmetics-state arrives before engine-ledger. Fixing the symptom on one path only is brittle the moment another side channel emerges. B) Resurrect `CosmeticUnlockEvaluator` (deleted in the R.7 correction) and wire it into the dispatch pipeline as a parallel granting path that walks `kCosmeticUnlockRules` for companions. Rejected: re-introduces the dual-pipeline state that the R.7 correction explicitly closed; we'd be carrying two granting flows again with no payoff over reading the inventory directly from one engine pass. C) Cross-reference the cosmetics inventory from `cosmetic_reveal_evaluator` to match the engine's achievement-based shape (change reveal to walk `NodeCompleted` instead of `Cond.ownsCosmetic`). Rejected: would make the reveal evaluator's hint-row UI lose the player-facing 'Získej Pečeť přísahy' copy that aligns with the existing ARB relic labels, in exchange for technical correctness on a check that semantically wants to talk about ownership. The engine moved to the inventory's truth, not the other way around. D) Add a new `MetaInPlayerInventory(cosmeticId, viaAchievement?)` condition that holds when EITHER the achievement completed OR the cosmetic is in inventory. Rejected: encodes the divergence as an OR-condition rather than fixing it. Two truth sources, one OR — a future drift would surface the same way.

decisions.title: R.8 — Periphery bundle: all three items "won't do — not actionable"
decisions.context: follow_ups.md §2 R.8 grouped three drobnosti that R.5 / R.6 / R.7 didn't subsume: (§2.12) a daily-quest periodKey legacy data audit (devtools panel that walks per-user Firestore engine collections and flags entries whose `periodKey` doesn't match `PeriodKey.fromRaw(stored).raw`); (§2.14) a Phase 3.c stylistic sweep that would rewrite `quest.id == 'literal'` to `quest.id == const ProgressionEntryId('literal')`; (§2.24) a `PlayerQuestLifecycle` timestamp enrichment that would populate `QuestCompletedPendingClaim.completedAt` + `QuestClaimed.claimedAt` from ledger event timestamps for relative-time UI hints. The DoD wording explicitly allowed "won't do — not actionable until a concrete trigger fires" as a valid close-out per item. R.8's job was to record each item's decision with its trigger so a future maintainer doesn't have to re-derive whether the work is still needed.
decisions.decision: Close all three items as "won't do — not actionable" with a written concrete trigger that would justify revisiting. Per item: §2.12 — no in-the-wild drift has been observed and Phase 2's UTC enforcement applies to new writes; the only pre-UTC documents would live on dev devices that ran the pre-Phase-2 build of the refactor branch (never shipped to users). Concrete trigger: an in-the-wild user reports a periodKey mismatch OR a devtools snapshot shows entries whose `periodKey != PeriodKey.fromRaw(stored).raw`. §2.14 — R.6 documented every remaining `untyped-id` site with a `lint-ignore` marker, which closes the visibility loop; the comparator-form rewrite (`==` with a typed const) is naturally subsumed by R.1's typed-id rollout for the call sites that needed it. Concrete trigger: a new untyped-id site appears at a file-touch boundary and the ratchet flags it. §2.24 — no UI surface in the current quests / cosmetics / chapter screens asks for relative-time hints; the `null` placeholder on the lifecycle timestamps is fine until one does. Concrete trigger: a design ask for relative-time copy (e.g., "claimed 2h ago") on a quest claim card or chapter completion summary. Zero code change. The decision lives in follow_ups.md §2 R.8 close-out block plus this ADR.
consequences: Track A R.8 closes with zero new code. The three items' rationale is preserved in two places (follow_ups.md inline + this ADR) so a future maintainer reading either one understands why nothing shipped and what would make them re-open the item.

Each item has an explicit concrete trigger. A drive-by maintainer can match an incoming bug report or feature request against the trigger and decide "this is the §2.12 trigger firing" without having to re-litigate the trade-off.

§2.12 in particular acknowledges a real edge case: dev builds of the refactor branch wrote pre-UTC periodKeys to local Firestore before Phase 2. If a dev device with that state happens to be the one a real user signs into via test build distribution, the orphan documents could surface. The trigger "a devtools snapshot shows drift" lets us catch this without proactively building the audit panel.

§2.14 is subsumed by R.1 + R.6. R.1 shipped typed extension types (`ProgressionEntryId`, `ObjectiveId`, `ChapterId`, `CosmeticId`, ...) and migrated the production call sites; R.6 documented every remaining raw-string boundary. The sweep would have rewritten comparator literals in tests + a handful of catalog content files, which is cosmetic — the typed IDs already exist at every site that exchanges them.

§2.24 is product-driven, not architectural. The lifecycle timestamps would be a wrapper around `event.timestamp` — trivial to add when a UI surface requests them, painful to maintain (timezone-aware formatting, locale handling, refresh cadence) when no surface uses them.
follow_ups.md §2 R.8 closing block lists the three items with their triggers. Track A summary table row R.8 marked ✅. Track A overall marked permanently closed 2026-05-19.
decisions.alternatives: A) Ship §2.12 (devtools periodKey audit panel) defensively. Rejected: building a UI panel + walk-loop + manual-cleanup tooling for an edge case nobody has reported is the kind of speculative work the Track A intro explicitly forbids ("Žádné 'přidám si to do follow_ups na později' — refactor se uzavírá, ne nafukuje"). The trigger-based revisit costs a few minutes of `git log` + ADR re-read when it fires; building the panel pre-emptively costs ~200 LoC + ongoing maintenance whether anyone uses it or not. B) Ship §2.14 (the typed-id sweep) anyway since R.6 already touched many files. Rejected: R.6 was a `lint-ignore`-marker pass with explicit-reason commentary; rewriting comparator forms is a different change shape (semantic equivalents that may be `const`-context-sensitive, requiring per-file judgement). Mixing the two would have ballooned R.6's diff and made each commit's intent unclear. The comparator form lands naturally at file-touch time per CLAUDE.md's "minimal targeted changes" principle. C) Ship §2.24 (lifecycle timestamps) speculatively in case a future UI wants them. Rejected: the `null` placeholders are sound (consumers pattern-match exhaustively per the sealed lifecycle invariant), and adding population logic with no consumer means writing untested timestamp-deriving code that will rot before the first relative-time surface lands. "Build it when the UI asks" is the cheaper sequence. D) Drop all three from follow_ups.md entirely. Rejected: the original audit captured non-trivial trade-offs (legacy data audit specifically); a future maintainer would re-derive the same trade-off without the historical record. The written close-out + concrete trigger preserves the option to revisit cheaply.

decisions.title: Track A — Domain refactor permanently closed
decisions.context: Track A in `docs/domain_model/follow_ups.md` enumerated eight items (R.1 → R.8) as the bounded, finite implementation round following the 22-phase domain refactor's archival (commit `bd5b004`, 2026-05-19). Each item shipped or closed as won't-do over the course of 2026-05-19, with atomic per-sub-PR commits and dedicated closing ADRs. The follow_ups document itself was the working-state record for the round and the project's CLAUDE.md close-out protocol explicitly directs that such working-state docs move into `archive/` alongside their predecessor plans once their scope closes.
decisions.decision: Mark Track A permanently closed and move `docs/domain_model/follow_ups.md` to `docs/domain_model/archive/follow_ups.md` alongside `archive/migration_plan.md`. Update internal links in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/domain_model/proposal.md` to point at the archived path. The eight items R.1 → R.8 are documented per-item via their own ADRs (`r1-catalog-domain-migration` through `r8-periphery-bundle-wont-do`); this ADR is the umbrella that records the close-out itself.
consequences: Track A closed: R.1 (catalog migration + typed cross-references), R.2 (NodeState cleanup), R.3.a/b/c (widget consumer migration), R.4 (repository contracts Result hardening), R.5.a/b/c (test pyramid hardening), R.6 (lint baselines to zero), R.7 (companion catalog audit), R.8 (periphery bundle). Total commits on branch `refactor/domain-model-design` from `main`: roughly 50. Test count 514 → 521 across the round (+7).
`follow_ups.md` archived. Future maintainers find the per-item rationale via the eleven Track A ADRs in `docs/site/data/decisions.json` and the archived plans under `docs/domain_model/archive/`.

Lint ratchets all at zero baseline. Any new violation must either be fixed or land with an explicit `lint-ignore` marker carrying a per-line reason. The discipline that took the codebase to zero is now the new default; growth is back to one violation at a time, each documented at the offending line.

Domain model permanently aligned with `proposal.md`. The Catalog ↔ Instance ↔ History triple, sealed lifecycles for the four entity kinds, first-class aggregates (Inventory, Loadout, EmblemBoard, GoalBoard, SocialPresence), the `Journal` interface + `LedgerSnapshot` read shape, and `Result<T, AppError>` at the outer data-layer boundaries are all in production. Future feature work consumes these contracts rather than re-deriving them.

Branch `refactor/domain-model-design` is ready for merge to `main`. The next architectural initiative starts from the closed Track A as its baseline; the parking-lot items in Track B (cloud-hosted catalogs, three-layer config system, persistence schema migration framework, V2 background notifications) are separate iterations with their own pre-conditions per the archived follow_ups Track B section.

Track C (decided-against items: provider rebuild granularity, cosmetic entitlements eventual consistency, Firestore codec strict mode, BackgroundSync exponential backoff) stays as a trigger-based revisit list. Each item has a written concrete trigger; none is actively scheduled.
decisions.alternatives: A) Keep follow_ups.md as a live document and continue adding items as new follow-ups surface. Rejected: the document's own §0 intro explicitly forbids this — "refactor se uzavírá, ne nafukuje" ("the refactor is closing, not growing"). Re-opening Track A would dilute the closure discipline that made the round bounded in the first place. Long-term initiatives go in Track B / Track C of the archived document, with their own pre-conditions; new architectural work starts as a new docs/<area>/<plan>.md per the close-out protocol in CLAUDE.md. B) Archive `follow_ups.md` but leave its links in CLAUDE.md / docs/architecture.md pointing at the live path. Rejected: would result in dead links the moment a future contributor moves the file. Updating the links in the same commit as the move keeps `docs/` self-consistent. C) Delete `follow_ups.md` entirely now that Track A closes. Rejected: the per-item rationale (Track B + Track C + Track D archive table) is historical context that a future architectural initiative reading the eleven Track A ADRs may want as cross-reference. Archive-don't-delete is the CLAUDE.md policy precisely for this reason.

decisions.title: PlayerStatistics jako sjednocený stat read API
decisions.context: Karta Trello #99 odhalila, že stat surfaces na home / quest / hero obrazovkách + expanded-card info banner každý fishují své číslo zvlášť — `ProgressionEngineProvider.currentStreakForDomain`, `streakForDomain(d).bestStreak`, `ledgerCounters.bestStreakByDomain`, ad-hoc map lookupy. Přidání nové metriky (total XP, level history, granted-reward tally, dist active days) by znamenalo patchovat tři až čtyři widgety. Agregáty samotné jsou rozházené přes dva value objekty: `EngineStreakSummary` (per-domain, per-objective) a `LedgerCounters` (per-rule reward counts, rolling windows, distinct active days).
decisions.decision: Zavést `PlayerStatistics` (immutable value object, `lib/features/progression_engine/domain/models/player_statistics.dart`) jako single read entry-point. Bundle: `Map<ProgressionDomain, EngineStreakSummary>` + `LedgerCounters` + `totalXp` + `level`. Provider drží `playerStatistics` getter, který rebuilduje fresh instanci po každém `_recomputeStreaks`. Helper `domainStreaks()` mapuje na flat per-domain rows pro UI cells. Empty sentinel pro pre-hydration null safety. Cloud sync intentionally out of scope — friend profiles dál čtou `SocialUserStats` Firestore wire formát; cloud-side stat materialisation patří do `JournalProjection` (Phase 20 domain refactoru).
consequences: Přidání nové metriky = jeden field na `PlayerStatistics` + jeden field na ledger producer + jeden consumer call. Žádné putování widget-by-widget.
Per-snapshot immutability: caller drží referenci na momentální stav; provider rebuilduje novou instanci na další tick. Žádné cross-snapshot delty (engine pipeline drží ordering).
Provider getter zachovává původní `currentStreakForDomain` / `streakForDomain` API pro backward compat — nové callers mají preferovat `playerStatistics`, staré callers se konvertují postupně.
Public na úrovni `domain/models/` — sealed-class-style sice ne (žádný discriminated union), ale `@immutable` + finální fields + `const empty` sentinel.
decisions.alternatives: Sealed `PlayerStatisticsView` s union typy per surface (HomeStats / QuestStats / HeroStats) — odmítnuto, je to jen agregace, ne výpočtová různorodost. Skip wrapper a používat existující providers napřímo — dále by se rozkládal a každá nová metrika by znamenala +1 getter na provider.

decisions.title: Goal revision history v SharedPreferences + Firestore mirror jako server truth
decisions.context: Karta Trello #99 zavedla `StreakBackfillService`, který přepočítává past-day completion events proti historickým goal targetům přes `GoalsProvider.progression*ForDate(day)`. Historie targetů žije v `SharedPreferences` pod klíči `goal_<metric>_history` jako JSON pole `{effectiveFrom, value}` revizí. Funguje to na jednom zařízení, ale fresh install / Google backup restore / sign-in na druhém zařízení historii ztratí — backfill spadne na current goal pro past days. To otevírá retroaktivní obcházení streaků: hráč si lokálně sníží goal, počká na backfill, a streak naskočí zpětně pro dny, kdy reálně nesplnil. Stejný attack vector pro libovolný daily-goal target.
decisions.decision: Lokální historie zůstává v `SharedPreferences` (per-metric JSON, ~10 řádků per metrika — Isar overhead by byl neúměrný). Zrcadlo v Firestore pod `users/{uid}/goal_history/{metricName}` jako document `{ revisions: [{target: double, effectiveAt: Timestamp}], updatedAt: serverTimestamp }`. Jeden doc per metrika (osm syncovaných metrik — `targetWeight` history nemá). Push při každém `GoalsProvider.set<Metric>` (best-effort, idempotent: doc je přepsán fresh state). Pull při `bindCloudUser` před `_runStreakBackfill`, merge union by `effectiveFrom` date, conflict → cloud wins (server truth). First-time migration: lokální history bez cloud counterpart se uploadne. Security rule `users/{uid}/{document=**}` gated na `request.auth.uid == uid` — žádné peer reads.
consequences: Fresh install / second device dostane historickou trail před backfillem; past-day completion events se vyhodnotí proti správnému targetu, ne proti current goalu.
Retroaktivní cheat zavřen pro hráče, který lokálně sníží goal — cloud drží original, merge cloud-wins ho přepíše zpátky před backfillem.
Per-metric doc šetří write fan-out (change v dailySteps netriggeruje rewrite ostatních sedmi metrik). Trade-off: 8 reads na sign-in místo 1.

Conflict resolution je jednoduchá (cloud wins). Edge case: hráč legitně změní goal na zařízení A a okamžitě jde offline na zařízení B — když se A push dokončí, B's lokální revision na stejný den se přepíše. Akceptováno; multi-device concurrent goal editing není priority use case.
Backward-compat: cloud bez historie → fallback na current goal (existing behavior, žádný regres pro pre-update users).

Re-trigger backfill po pull: `_pullCloudLedger` volá `goalsProvider.pullAndMergeCloudHistory(uid)` před `unawaited(refresh())`, který automaticky pustí `_runStreakBackfill` s updated history. Žádný explicitní re-trigger hook potřeba.

Firestore rules deploy je all-or-nothing: `firestore.rules` v gitu pokrývá pouze `goal_history` + existující engine ledger / cosmetic owner-only subcollections. Public collections (`handles`, `friend_requests`, `friendships`, `achievement_shares`, `users/{uid}` doc, cross-user `notifications` writes) jsou explicitně mimo scope — soubor NENÍ wired do `firebase.json` deploy target a produkční pravidla zatím žijí v Firebase Console. Header rules souboru tohle dokumentuje; deploy musí počkat na samostatnou social-rules kartu s emulator coverage.
decisions.alternatives: (1) Migrovat history do Isar — odmítnuto, dnes ~50 řádků data per user, JSON v prefs je dostačující a Firestore wire mapping je přímý nad existujícím formátem. (2) Jeden doc `users/{uid}/profile/goal_history` se vším — méně docs ale větší write fan-out (jedna změna = rewrite všeho). (3) Per-revision append-only (Firestore subcollection s doc per revision) — overkill pro 10 řádků dat, drahé čtení. (4) Skip cloud sync a spoléhat na lokální history — odmítnuto, právě tohle otevírá cheat path.
